item: Station staffing set by demand in 2027 contracts
basis: ATU location-based staffing covers ~11% of BART's workforce, mostly station agents plus some foreworkers and analysts (BART response to grand jury, p. 23): ~505 of 4,599 FTEs (BART, Train Automation Facts); 15-25% fewer positions through attrition at ~$163K each, BART's FY27 cost per train operator including overtime ($81-83M for 503), since station agents share the operators' pay scale (ATU contract S47.1; foreworkers earn more, so this errs low); ~1/3 redeployed to platforms and trains. Corrected Nov 11 2026: first published as ~470 positions at ~$190K each, ~$9-15M

basis: Train operator wages, benefits and overtime are $81-83M in the FY27 preliminary budget for 503 operators (BART, Train Automation Facts); keeping ~20-45% of that cost for roving attendants and control staff leaves ~$45-65M; capital costs such as platform doors, and their upkeep, not included.
